populations.
What is food fortiﬁcation?
The Codex Alimentarius deﬁnes food fortiﬁcation or enrichment as the addition of micronutrients to foods, whether or not they are
normally contained in the food, for the purposes of preventing or correcting a demonstrated micronutrient deﬁciency. The Codex
also notes that the quantity of micronutrients to add should be sufﬁcient to correct or prevent deﬁciency when the food is consumed
in normal amounts by the population at risk, but not likely to result in excessive intakes by individuals with high intake of the forti-
ﬁed food (Codex Alimentarius, 2015). These recommendations are applicable to single foods.
